articles.title: Luka Doncic injury update: JJ Redick provides 'cautious' update on Lakers’ leader’s status against Clippers
articles.summary: Luka Doncic is out for the Lakers’ game against the Clippers on Wednesday night because of back tightness.
articles.body: Luka Doncic is out for the Lakers’ game against the Clippers on Wednesday night because of back tightness. Coach JJ Redick said the guard and Ziaire Williams both woke up sore, a day after Doncic scored 41 points in a loss to Portland. Tuesday’s 136-129 result was the Lakers’ first loss of the year. Los Angeles is calling the move a precaution. It is his first missed game this season, and the Lakers are in the middle of five games in seven days.Why is Luka Doncic not playing against the Clippers?Luka Doncic is sitting out the second night of the Lakers’ first back-to-back this season. Redick said Doncic and Williams both woke up with problems, tightness in the back for one and soreness in the left foot for the other. The coach pointed to a tough run of games with little rest in between and kept the explanation short: “Just being overly cautious.”The reigning scoring champion leads the NBA at 36.0 points per game and has topped 40 points twice in four games. Against Portland, Doncic played 37 minutes and finished with 41 points on 12-of-22 shooting, five rebounds and nine assists. The tightness first appeared on the injury report for the second night of the back-to-back, and nothing in the reporting ties it to a particular play.Dan Woike of The Athletic added that a source sees “No longterm worry” for Doncic.What does Doncic’s absence mean for the Lakers this week?Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler are expected to carry the Lakers against a Clippers team that is 1-2 and has six players out, including Bradley Beal, Brandon Ingram and Rui Hachimura. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton could see bigger roles. Williams, Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr are also out for Los Angeles, which beat the Clippers 125-117 last week.The bigger question is Friday. The Lakers open NBA Cup play at Golden State on Oct. 30, and Redick would say only that playing both Doncic and Williams is the hope. Home games against Toronto on Nov. 1 and Miami on Nov. 2 finish the five-in-seven run.Back issues are not new. Doncic missed a short stretch with lower-back tightness in March 2021 while in Dallas, and those episodes cleared in a game or two. The more serious injury was a Grade 2 left hamstring strain in April, which ended the 2025-26 season early and cost Doncic the playoff run.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: M23 Rebels: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over Congo war
articles.summary: Congo accuses Rwanda of backing M23 rebels and plundering minerals in its conflict hit East
articles.body:
The United States has imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops and halt support for the rebels.

"Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

The sanctions come months after Rwanda and DR Congo signed a US-brokered peace agreement aimed at ending the conflict.

Fighting has continued in eastern DR Congo since early 2025, when M23 seized the cities of Goma and Bukavu. Rwanda denies backing M23.

The US Treasury says Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training.

The M23 has seized mineral-rich areas, including gold-mining sites in South Kivu and Rubaya, a major coltan-producing area in North Kivu. Washington says minerals from rebel-held territory enter Rwanda's supply chains, alleging that Rwanda exports more minerals than it produces.

Inside the Congolese mine vital to mobile phones, as rebels give BBC rare access

The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo

The sanctions are intended to reinforce the Washington Accords, signed by the Congolese and Rwandan presidents in December 2025 under US mediation. The deal aimed to end the conflict and expand regional trade and investment, but fighting has continued.

On 24 October, ahead of the sanctions announcement, DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi urged the international community to increase pressure on Rwanda.

"We must firmly demand that the international community impose concrete sanctions against Rwanda and exert increased pressure, so that we may finally secure a lasting peace in our country," he said.

In a statement to Reuters, DR Congo foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and urged Rwanda to honour its commitments under the Washington Accords, respect the UN Charter and withdraw its troops from Congolese territory.

"The Washington Accords contain clear commitments regarding Rwanda's security, specifically the neutralization of the DR Congo-sponsored FDLR genocidal militia, which are wholly unmet, and with no accountability," Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo told the BBC.

The FDLR is a militia linked to perpetrators of Rwanda's 1994 genocide. Kigali considers it a security threat and cites its presence in eastern DR Congo to justify its military posture.

"Rwanda remains ready to fully implement the Washington Accords, concurrently with the willingness of the DRC to fulfill those commitments, and with the mediator holding all parties accountable," she said.

The US also sanctioned Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a popular bank and financial institution serving Rwanda's security services.

Washington alleges it facilitated tens of millions of dollars in transactions for M23 and its political wing, the Congo River Alliance, helped pay for military equipment for Rwandan forces from China and enabled gold to be transported from rebel-controlled areas to Kigali.

The sanctions freeze the designated entities' assets under US jurisdiction and generally prohibit US individuals and businesses from conducting transactions with them, unless authorised or exempt. Violations can result in penalties for US and foreign parties.

The measures follow earlier US sanctions against Rwanda's army and four senior military commanders in March 2026. The US imposed further sanctions on Gasabo gold refinery and three mining companies accused of smuggling conflict minerals in June 2026.

Pressure is also mounting over Rwanda's international sports partnerships. Two US senators have urged the National Basketball Association (NBA) to reconsider its commercial relations with Kigali, questioning whether it aligns with the league's stated commitment to human rights.

In a letter sent to NBA commissioner Adam Silver on 23 October, senators Jeff Merkley and Marsha Blackburn questioned the league's continued partnership with Rwanda amid allegations of human rights abuses.

The NBA has yet to issue a substantive response to the letter.

Rwanda has used sports high-profile sports sponsorship to raise its international profile. Early this month, it secured a 10-year deal to host Formula 1's African Grand Prix in the early 2030s.

The country's sponsorship of Arsenal ended in 2026, while Bayern Munich has also ended its commercial partnership with Visit Rwanda.

The M23 has recently joined a new rebel coalition, known as the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) and led by former Congolese President Joseph Kabila, which wants to oust Tshisekedi's government.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Game 6 live on Sky Sports, Thursday at 4.30pm as Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream makes history
articles.summary: Golden State Valkryies travel to Atlanta Dream for Game 6 of WNBA Finals, leading series 3-2; a win will seal the championship in their second year of existence; Atlanta seek history-making Game 7; Watch Game 6 of the WNBA Finals, live on Sky Sports from 4.30pm, Thursday
articles.body:
Amid scheduling drama, which has resulted in a 12.30pm tip off time in Atlanta - and 9.30am in San Francisco - the match is still a sell out and much anticipated.

"I'd like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said in jest this week.

"I hope everybody gets to see it, somehow. I know for some people, it's not realistic. They have jobs. They won't be able to make it. I'm disappointed for that, but I'm really hopeful that as many people can see the game as possible."

The game could have been played at Atlanta's 'usual' home court at the Gateway Center Arena on Thursday night. It would have been a great atmosphere, but nobody wanted the tiny crowd of 3,500 or so.

In the future, State Farm and its 17,000 capacity will become the full-time home of the Dream, which means potential WNBA Finals dates won't clash with Atlanta Hawks NBA games.

"It's better than, you know, having it at the YMCA that night in front of 75 people," the NBA's Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. "They're doing what they've got to do."

The Valkyries, for their part, have some ideas on how fans can manage the early start time.

"Call in sick," guard Veronica Burton said. "I recommend it."

Forward Kiah Stokes added: "Don't y'all know how to fake a cough?"

The players have handled it with a sense of humour. So too has Smesko, with his tongue-in-cheek plea for a national holiday to be declared.

Continued growth in record-breaking year for WNBA

Game 6 will serve as either the last game, or the next-to-last game, in a season that the WNBA can point to as a sign of continued growth.

There were more games than ever, which meant that more people showed up than ever - around 3.8 million and counting this season, including playoffs.

The average number of fans per game will end up around 11,500, another record and up about 4.5 per cent over the previous season.

Las Vegas star A'ja Wilson won her record fifth MVP award. The league set records for points and three-pointers per game. A new star was born, with Minnesota's Olivia Miles the unanimous pick as rookie of the year.

Atlanta's Angel Reese was named defensive player of the year, while in Indiana, Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark scored more points than any WNBA backcourt ever in a season.

The playoffs too were unpredictable, and will end with a new champion crowned. But it's just a case of whether it will happen at Game 6 on Thursday?

articles.title: Chus Bueno, sobre NBA Europa: "Los clubes están abiertos a entrar, pero quieren entrar todos"
articles.standfirst: "Me hubiese gustado llegar antes para trabajar juntos (con la NBA) desde la concepción del modelo. Ahora hay dos modelos muy diferentes e intentar llegar a un acuerdo es más difícil"
articles.summary: "Me hubiese gustado llegar antes para trabajar juntos (con la NBA) desde la concepción del modelo. Ahora hay dos modelos muy diferentes e intentar llegar a un acuerdo es más difícil"
articles.body: El director general de la Euroliga, Chus Bueno, explica en una entrevista con EFE que los 13 equipos propietarios de dicha competición están "abiertos" a entrar en un hipotético torneo creado junto a la NBA, siempre que entren todos, mantengan el control sobre el mismo y se rebajen las cantidades de ingreso que exige la liga profesional americana. "Si quieren entrar en Europa y formar una alianza con nosotros, los clubes tienen que formar parte de este modelo y tienen que discutirse las cantidades. Es una discusión que está encima de la mesa. Los clubes están abiertos a entrar, pero quieren entrar todos y ver las mejores fórmulas para no invertir tanto", ha señalado. Bueno (Barcelona, 1969) es un hombre de baloncesto. Jugó en la ACB entre 1988 y 1994, fue director general de la Federación Española de Baloncesto (FEB) entre 2006 y 2010, y vicepresidente de la NBA en Europa, África y Oriente Medio durante 12 años, además de director de la liga estadounidense en España, entre otros cargos. Bien relacionado con la cúpula actual de la liga americana, en febrero fue elegido CEO de la Euroliga, con el reto de acelerar su crecimiento económico y de lidiar con la intención unilateral de la NBA de desembarcar en Europa de la mano de la FIBA, enemistada con la máxima competición de clubes desde su separación en el año 2000. "Me hubiese gustado llegar antes para trabajar juntos (con la NBA) desde la concepción del modelo. Ahora hay dos modelos muy diferentes e intentar llegar a un acuerdo es más difícil", lamenta. Bueno reconoce que en la NBA "saben mucho de marketing, de generar valor de marca y tienen mucha experiencia global", por lo que podrían "ayudar a acelerar el crecimiento de la Euroliga", pero reivindica que ésta tiene una "infraestructura" en el continente de la que la NBA carece: "Tenemos la capacidad y la experiencia para operar en un ecosistema diverso, y a los mejores clubes y aficiones". Estas declaraciones llegan tres semanas después de que los trece clubes propietarios de la Euroliga (Anadolu Efes, Baskonia, CSKA Moscú, Armani Olimpia Milán, Barça, Bayern Múnich, Fenerbahçe, Asvel, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Olympiacos, Panathinaikos, Real Madrid y Zalgiris Kaunas) rechazaran la primera propuesta de la NBA que, según pudo confirmar entonces EFE, ofrecía más de 500 millones de euros a repartir entre dichos clubes y exigía una inversión de 440 millones a cada uno de los interesados en sumarse al nuevo proyecto. En dicho encuentro sí se aprobó la conversión de las licencias de los propietarios en franquicias y continuar el proceso de expansión de la Euroliga, de 20 a 24 equipos a partir del curso 2026-27. "Si hay otras propuestas de la NBA, nuestras líneas están abiertas, pero seguiremos trabajando en el modelo de la Euroliga", valora Bueno. Aunque apela a la confidencialidad para no tratar las cifras de la primera oferta de la NBA, el director general de la Euroliga expone que los trece clubes fundadores "llevan 26 años invirtiendo y creando un producto que cuenta con 94 millones de aficionados y que hace de la Euroliga una marca potente", algo que "tiene un valor". Bueno también responde a las recientes declaraciones del subcomisionado de la NBA, Mark Tatum, quien aseguró que el modelo financiero de NBA Europa proyecta distribuir a los clubes el triple de dinero en comparación con los planes de negocio a diez años de la Euroliga, que prevé repartir 3.400 millones entre los propietarios (2.200 de ingresos y 1.200 de las cuotas de nuevas franquicias). "No es así. Por ejemplo, si (con NBA Europa) las franquicias ponen 500 millones y en diez años ganan 240, todavía pierden 260 millones. En nuestro caso, no pierden dinero, porque no ponen nada. Si generan 100 o 200, eso generan", ilustra el CEO de la Euroliga. Por otra parte, Bueno remarca que los clubes no cederán el poder de decisión a un actor externo: "Los clubes tienen una posición muy clara, querrán ser parte de la toma de decisiones. Han creado una liga de la que son los propietarios y quieren seguir decidiendo su futuro". Asimismo, subraya que la NBA "omite intencionadamente" a la Euroliga y su segunda competición asociada, la Eurocopa, en sus proyecciones, y que la creación de una nueva competición, si no involucra a todos los equipos, generará "mucha más fragmentación" en vez de "ordenar el mercado" europeo, como defienden los americanos. "La Euroliga y la Eurocopa no van a desaparecer. Ya hay clubes que me han dicho: 'Si llegas a un acuerdo con la NBA y nos dejas fuera, crearemos nuestra propia competición'. Si no solucionamos el problema para todos, tendremos más competiciones, se llamen como se llamen", apunta. Con todo, el máximo ejecutivo de la Euroliga celebra que el modelo de las franquicias, "de una competición muy amplia y fuerte", ha llegado para quedarse. "Los clubes han cambiado la mentalidad, quieren estabilidad y no renunciarán a este estatus", afirma. Según su plan de negocio, la transición al modelo de franquicias triplicará el valor de los clubes que actualmente cuentan con licencia (de 1.800 a 5.400 millones) y multiplicará por 5,7 el de la Liga (de 1.400 a 7.980 millones) en una década. No obstante, la Euroliga afronta el reto de que todos sus clubes sean sostenibles económicamente dentro de una década, una condición que ahora cumple solo el 40%. Para lograrlo, no solo pretende modernizar los pabellones e incrementar los ingresos, sino también perfeccionar un sistema de 'fair play' al que algunos equipos "quieren darle una vuelta más". "La próxima semana tenemos una reunión para tratar sobre esto, que los que tengan dinero puedan seguir gastando, pero también equilibrar el sistema para que no tenga un efecto inflacionista ni arriesgue el objetivo de la sostenibilidad", comenta Bueno, quien admite que "siempre va a haber diferencias" por la disparidad fiscal entre los países participantes.

articles.title: Their record is strong. Their roster is battered. Can the Thunder still contend for an NBA title despite injuries?
articles.summary: Oklahoma City lost two key players — Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace — in the first month of the season to injuries.
articles.body: The Oklahoma City Thunder’s win on opening night of the new NBA season was a reminder of everything that makes the league’s 2025 champion a prime contender to win again. Barely one week later, those aspirations have already been damaged. Thunder star Jalen Williams, the team’s second-leading scorer and best all-around defender during its title run two seasons ago, fractured a fibula and dislocated his left ankle in a gruesome injury Sunday. The same night, Cason Wallace, a hounding defender and accurate shooter in his own right, tore the labrum in his shoulder. Thunder general manager Sam Presti didn’t specify how long both will miss, but they are expected to miss months, at a minimum, putting their availability for any playoff run — especially a deep one — in serious doubt. Jeff Stotts, an athletic trainer who runs a site that tracks sports injuries, wrote that since 2005, just one player had sustained a torn labrum like Wallace’s and returned later that season. “We’ll get them back, we’ll get them healthy, but we got a lot of basketball to play in front of us,” Presti said Monday. “We got to put it together, figure out what the next steps are, because this is part of the business that we’re in.” Getting Williams back healthy had been central to Oklahoma City’s goal of returning to the NBA Finals. Injuries sidelined Williams for more than half of last season, and he also missed time during last season’s Western Conference finals, which the Thunder lost in seven games to San Antonio. When San Antonio and Oklahoma City met on opening night, with Oklahoma City winning on the road, it was widely seen as a preview of the spring, when the two teams with loaded rosters featuring superstars still in their 20s were expected again to face off for the right to make the Finals. “It’s obviously going to be tough without a player” like Williams, Thunder guard and two-time league MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said. “But he’s not gone forever. He’ll be back better than ever, and we know it. We’ve just got to hold the fort down until he comes back.” The Thunder aren’t the only team whose season has already been upended by injuries. Minnesota Timberwolves All-Star guard Anthony Edwards is expected to miss around two months after his right knee required an arthroscopic procedure, ESPN reported. A right knee injury will also sideline Utah Jazz star forward Jaren Jackson Jr. for a reported six to eight weeks, while an ankle injury will sideline Orlando Magic star Paolo Banchero at least a month. Indiana Pacers All-Star Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) and Orlando guard Jalen Suggs (right knee) also will miss time. Drawing a connection between some of the acute injuries, like Williams’ freak fracture, and cumulative injuries such as the knee that has bothered Edwards for months is difficult, said Dr. Tarek Souryal, a former president of the NBA Physicians Association who was the Dallas Mavericks’ team doctor for more than two decades. “What you’re witnessing is most likely a statistical aberration, not necessarily evidence of a systemic problem,” Souryal said. “A cluster of injuries, however unusual or alarming, does not by itself establish a causal relationship.” Wallace and Williams are homegrown talents, drafted and developed by Oklahoma City into centerpieces of the 2025 championship team. The Thunder, under Presti, drafted and traded so well that their depth was often unparalleled around the NBA, with capable emerging contributors backing up more established starters. The current collective bargaining agreement between the league and the players union, however, makes it financially difficult for a team to keep together a core of players for longer than a few seasons once they get old enough, and perform well enough, to command lucrative long-term extensions. The Thunder are one of the league’s prime examples; last summer, as expensive contracts owed to their star trio of Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Chet Holmgren began to hit their payroll, the team jettisoned some of its key rotation players in financially motivated moves so as not to trigger onerous penalties. Wallace, however, wasn’t someone the team felt it could part with; it signed him to a five-year, $139 million extension in mid-October. Those offseason moves, combined with the injuries, have withered the depth that had allowed Presti to be patient in trade negotiations during previous seasons, without feeling a need to make splashy midseason acquisitions. An executive for an NBA team said rivals were quickly monitoring whether the Thunder’s position would change in light of how much their rotation had been depleted only a week into the season. “It’s tough from a compassion standpoint. Those are guys that work so hard, they’re such great players, so that was a tough pill,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said. “The guys did a great job of appropriately honoring that and also getting themselves ready to compete, ready to play. They heard from [Williams]. They saw Cason. So it allowed them to feel good about going out there and competing for the team.” Four games into the season, despite the injuries, Oklahoma City was an unbeaten 4-0. How long it can remain atop the West, however, has become one of the key stories of the young season.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long redemption road in China
articles.summary: French star at the centre of controversy after a video appeared to show him making fun of former Chinese leader Mao.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the French striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China will not be easily or quickly repaired, experts say.

The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a controversy after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao.

Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face digitally altered onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China.

He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing.

Leading Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV’s schedule.

Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said.

China is the world’s second-biggest economy and most lucrative market. Within two days, as the video, purportedly filmed in April, circulated online, the striker , his club Real Madrid and La Liga apologised.

A spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously” .

“Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told the AFP news agency.

“It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China.

“In the age of the mobile internet, things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high.

“An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story.

“It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.”

The furore and the fallout are not an unfamiliar tale .

Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.

China effectively cut ties with the National Basketball Association (NBA) in the United States in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters.

NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said.

Basketball is among the most popular sports in China along with football. However, Morey’s remark saw the NBA wiped from CCTV for more than a year.

NBA preseason matches returned to China only last year.

Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case – and now Mbappe’s – an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split.

No way back for Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga?

Spanish football also has a lot to lose.

A source within La Liga told AFP that China and the US alone finance the “majority” of international broadcasting rights, which were valued at 748 million euros ($834m) for the 2024-25 season.

According to the Real Madrid-affiliated newspaper Marca, the Madrid club generates 10 to 15 percent of its jersey and other merchandise sales in China.

Real Madrid also counts Chinese companies among its main sponsors, with Hisense, sports betting firm Kaiyun Sports and Linglong Tire all featuring prominently.

Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said showing fast and heartfelt remorse was the first step.

“This will influence the decision on whether to continue the broadcast ban and, if so, for how long,” he told AFP.

Sports commentator Yan cast doubt on whether the reputation of Mbappe, whose face has adorned drink bottles and advertising campaigns in China, can ever fully recover.

“Judging by commercial sponsorships and big ad campaigns he appeared in during the World Cup, he has a huge influence in China,” he said.

“If that influence can’t be sustained, there can be no talk of commercial interests, and La Liga and Real Madrid will definitely be badly affected.”

Yan said it was “genuinely hard to predict” what happens next.

“In the short term, I’m certainly not optimistic,” he added.

“If they want to repair their image and the relationship, their future actions and behaviour will be key.”

articles.title: MATT CALKINS: Media keeps calling women's sports advocates 'anti-trans' without a shred of proof
articles.summary: A Washington Post column labeled women's sports advocacy as "anti-trans," but Sophie Cunningham and others say the framing is a media-driven lie.
articles.body: I saw it right there in the lede of a Washington Post column Tuesday. "A transgender girl stretched for a high school race as supporters of a new anti-trans ballot measure chanted 'enough is enough'." I saw it six days earlier in a Guardian headline about how doctors are fighting an "anti-trans measure" that would separate biological girls from boys in women's sports. The Portland Mercury got in on it, too, writing in its Monday headline how "anti-trans activists" attempted to overshadow the Thorns' playoff-clinching win. These aren't columnists offering subjective opinions. These are media outlets writing opinions as fact. The message? You can't possibly be a women's sports advocate without being transphobic. And that thought is just ... tired. WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE I have no doubt there are people who have genuine scorn for members of the trans community. Every group — men, women, Whites, Blacks, gays, Muslims, Jews. etc. — has its haters. But the voices backing these ballot measures? The figures advocating for girls' and women's spaces? They aren't demonizing trans people. Not in the slightest. Perhaps the most famous face to speak up on this issue in the past few months is Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who said in an ESPN interview: "I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men." But she prefaced that very sentence by saying "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that.' I think that I am here to extend love." A few days after that interview came out, a high school girl in Seattle named Ahnaleigh Wilson — holding a sign saying "Thank You Sophie For Speaking Up For Girls" — echoed Cunningham's sentiment, saying "I don’t hate trans people and I have nothing against them. I just think that girls should have their own sports." SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM COMMENDS WASHINGTON STATE GIRLS WHO WALKED OFF CROSS COUNTRY RACE OVER MALE TEAMMATE Fellow Washingtonian Frances Staudt — who says she's been harassed constantly for refusing to play a high school basketball game against a boy — added "There’s only so many times that I can say that what we are standing up for is not anti-trans. This is pro-women’s sports." Yet the headlines have kept coming. From Colorado Newsline: "Signatures submitted for anti-trans Colorado ballot measures." From Politico: "Democrats revamp their midterm playbook for GOP's anti-trans attacks." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE From Ms. Magazine: "This Midterm Season, Five States Are Voting on Anti-Trans Ballot." If you read these stories, you'll notice that none give examples of someone issuing a slur or insult. They just presume that a bill or person opposing certain demands from members of the trans community is "anti-trans." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's pretty glaring when and how the media chooses to use the word "anti." When Colin Kaepernick wore pig socks and compared cops to modern-day slave patrol, did "anti-police" headlines from legacy media come flooding in? What about when BLM protesters chanted "Pigs in a blanket, fry 'em like bacon!" That was pure vitriol toward their opponents. You simply don't see that type of rhetoric from the separate-men-and-women-in-sports crowd. And by the way, that crowd includes Caitlyn Jenner — perhaps the most famous transgender person in the world. It includes Ari Laureano, a detransitioned male who was kicked out of a Portland Thorns game last week for his XX-XY shirt. The biggest misnomer in this debate is that supporters of biological female-only spaces in sports and locker rooms all have animus toward trans people. But the media keeps repeating the lie that they do. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Makes sense, I suppose. When you don't have the truth, repetition is your best weapon.

articles.title: NBA Rookies Already Looking Like Draft Steals After 1 Week
articles.summary: Four different players have won the NBA MVP award in the last eight years. Only one of them, Joel Embiid, was a top-10 pick. That's a pretty good indicator that hidden gems are always available later in the draft—provided teams know where to look.
articles.body:
Four different players have won the NBA MVP award in the last eight years. Only one of them, Joel Embiid, was a top-10 pick. That's a pretty good indicator that hidden gems are always available later in the draft—provided teams know where to look.

The 2026 class certainly has its share of high-performing lottery picks, but it's already clear that a ton of talent came off the board outside the top 10. In fact, a couple of big-time early contributors lasted until the second round.

A week into the 2026-27 season, let's check in on a few of the biggest steals in the draft. From Yaxel Lendeborg and Aday Mara, who should have gone much higher in the lottery, to Trevon Brazile and Meleek Thomas, who had no business slipping into the second round, this rookie class is loaded.

The old adage that "you either win or you learn" certainly applies to NBA rookies. Yaxel Lendeborg is doing a whole lot of learning as he plays a major role for the Golden State Warriors.

Averages of 21.8 points, 9.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists through his first four games clearly show the impact the No. 11 pick is making. His breakout effort against the Denver Nuggets to help the Warriors win their first game of the season on Oct. 26 suggested first-option potential.

But the lessons of his first week matter more. For example, Lendeborg learned earlier in the year that irritating Luka Dončić is probably a bad idea .

Another teaching moment came from Warriors head coach Steve Kerr, who used some of Lendeborg's directness with the media to call out the rookie's major issues with team defense.

Lendeborg's size, skill and competitiveness are all major assets that have him performing like a top-five rookie most nights. Imagine what he'll be capable of once he makes some adjustments to his trash-talk targets and off-ball instincts.

Allen Graves may never be a high-volume scorer or go-to option, but he's already showing basically every other skill you'd want in a role-playing starter.

The No. 19 pick can lock down offensive opponents of all shapes and sizes, making him a perfect fit for the Toronto Raptors' smothering defensive scheme. Check him out stymying Trae Young:

Graves is a true "little things" superstar, gifted with innate timing and anticipation that basically allows him to teleport to the right spot for rebounds and loose balls. He has tremendous hands and excellent length at 6'9", both of which help compensate for limited run-and-jump athleticism.

Though he's only in a small rotation role right now, the Raptors may find it increasingly difficult to keep him off the floor. Very few players sustain their effectiveness when scaling up in minutes, but Graves could lose plenty from his per-minute figures and still make a massive impact.

He's averaging 14.1 points, 10.2 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 3.9 blocks and 1.6 steals per 36 minutes through his first three games.

Few teams needed an infusion of athleticism and activity more than the Denver Nuggets, who were short on both qualities before losing Peyton Watson over the summer.

Trevon Brazile, a springy 6'10" big with a 9'1" standing reach, is more than filling the void.

An absolute menace on the glass, the No. 35 pick is constantly darting around the floor in pursuit of rebounds. He averaged 16.1 boards per 36 minutes (4.6 offensive) in his first two professional games. As an added bonus, he's at least acting like a player who'll also bring perimeter value.

Twelve of Brazile's first 19 career field-goal attempts came from long distance. He only hit three of them, but the ball comes out of his hands smoothly and with plenty of arc. There's a chance he develops into a potent interior weapon who can also stretch the floor.

As the league learns Brazile needs to be boxed out at all costs, it'll become harder for him to hustle his way to so many boards and loose balls. But if the intensity he's shown in the early going does result in opponents paying more attention to him, it'll free up his more established, starry teammates to operate freely.

This one is more about the eye test than production, as No. 12 pick Aday Mara is only averaging 14.5 minutes per game for the Oklahoma City Thunder.

In that limited action, the 7'2" center is displaying a highly unusual combination of size and touch that would have him occupying a much larger role on a team that didn't already have three established bigs ahead of him in the rotation.

Even with Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein and Jaylin Williams in the way, Mara seems bound to carve out more playing time. His length and feel makes him an excellent finisher around the basket. He runs the floor extremely well for his size. Mara can defend the rim and, perhaps most intriguingly, possesses legitimate passing vision.

Mara's intuitive ability to move the ball may not seem necessary on an offense with two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and emerging playmaker Ajay Mitchell, but OKC just lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace from the wing rotation. That could create an all-hands-on-deck approach, at least off the bench, that might allow Mara to tap into his tantalizing facilitation skills.

In the Thunder's first game without J-Dub and Wallace, the Michigan product racked up career highs with 19 minutes, 11 points, 10 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 blocks. Perhaps that's a sign of things to come.

Meleek Thomas' NBA debut didn't come until the third game of the season, but the No. 34 pick certainly delivered when finally called upon.

Thomas' 16 points came in just 19 minutes of an overtime win against the previously undefeated Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 26. Without the 20-year-old guard's game-salvaging stint in the first quarter, the contest probably wouldn't have gone to an extra period.

"We didn't have energy, we were flat, we were playing the wrong way," Donovan Mitchell told reporters after the win. "We weren't doing the right things, and for him to be the spark in his first game of the year, like, it's not normal."

Thomas was the scoring leader during Summer League, averaging 27.2 points per game and hitting 43.8 percent of his long-range attempts. Veteran teammates quickly bought in during preseason, but a backcourt populated by All-NBA talents meant Thomas was going to have a hard time earning minutes.

If he continues to make the most of his opportunities, the DNPs he logged during his first two games will become a thing of the past.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: Grading Every NBA Team After Wild First Week
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA season has already given us some great basketball (and some unfortunate injuries) as we begin to get a feel for how all 30 teams will shake out.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season has already given us some great basketball (and some unfortunate injuries) as we begin to get a feel for how all 30 teams will shake out.

Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat are downright bad now, while Ja Morant, LaMelo Ball, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James are thriving in new situations.

Both the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs have stumbled out of the gate following their appearances in the NBA Finals, and one recent champion should be in full-out panic mode right now.

It's time to pass out some early report card grades for every NBA team following a whirlwind of a first week.

Note: All records and stats are accurate as of Oct. 27.

We saw a glimpse of how special this Atlanta Hawks team can be on both ends in a 128-81 thumping of the (now 3-1) Charlotte Hornets.

The Hawks (now equipped with Lu Dort off their bench) held the Hornets to just 11-of-51 shooting from three (22 percent) while only one Charlotte starter registered more than six points.

A win over the Orlando Magic and some respectable losses to a good Houston Rockets team shouldn't hurt our confidence in Atlanta, a team that's perhaps deeper than any version we saw in the Trae Young era.

With the Hawks currently top-eight in both offense and defense to begin the year, fans should feel good (although maybe not great) about their team so far.

A 3-1 record with a lone loss to a good Detroit Pistons team looks decent on the surface, but these Boston Celtics are far from a championship team right now.

Paul George is carrying a large offensive load (22.3 points) but will inevitably miss time at some point. The Celtics needed overtime to beat a bad Brooklyn Nets team at home and Jayson Tatum is struggling from three right now (24.1 percent).

There's still talent here, but Boston looks like the lite version of the squad that won the 2024 title.

This is going to be a long, sad season for Brooklyn Nets fans.

An 0-4 record to start the year isn't all that surprising, even with the additions of players like Julius Randle, Keon Ellis and No. 6 overall pick Mikel Brown Jr., who's shooting just 28.6 percent overall in his first three games.

Yes, the Nets kept it close against teams like the Boston Celtics and Cleveland Cavaliers, although developing the team's young talent is more important than overall record. Of the seven first-round picks that Brooklyn has made over the past two years, only one (Brown) is averaging more than 10 points per game to begin the season.

With zero wins to date and little progression from the team's young talent, the Nets only get a D for some close losses.

Week 1 Grades for Top Stars On New Teams 🌟

The Charlotte Hornets got throttled by the Atlanta Hawks in their home opener, but other than that the season has been a success thus far.

A 3-1 record is very respectable, especially considering both Kon Knueppel and Coby White have yet to make their season debuts due to injury. Naz Reid (19.5 points, 41.2 percent from three) and Grayson Allen (16.8 points, 48.3 percent from three) have been terrific pickups, and the Miles Bridges trade looks like a huge win for Charlotte.

Simply treading water without their two best guards would be a success for the Hornets, who have exceeded expectations to this point.

Saying the Chicago Bulls have been hot garbage is an insult to high-temperature trash everywhere.

Yes, the Bulls have managed to win a game, albeit against the Milwaukee Bucks. Chicago still ranks dead last in the NBA in offense (101.8 rating) and net rating ( minus-18.3 ), as they've already suffered multiple losses of 35 points or more.

Starting point guard Josh Giddey is averaging just 7.0 points on 33.3 percent shooting overall and 15.4 percent from three, Norman Powell and Matas Buzelis are both shooting under 39.0 percent and rookie Caleb Wilson clearly looks like the team's best player (not a good thing).

No one was penciling the Bulls in as a playoff team in the East this season, but growth was expected. So far, Chicago looks worse than ever.

It's been a roller coaster of a season already for the Cleveland Cavaliers, one that began in their very first game.

The Cavs looked unstoppable in the first half of their season opener against the high-powered Philadelphia 76ers, as Cleveland built a 29-point halftime lead only to see Philly come all the way back and win the game.

The Cavaliers also nearly blew a double-digit home lead vs. the Brooklyn Nets before taking down a very good Minnesota Timberwolves team in overtime.

James Harden is starting to show his age, shooting just 35.1 percent overall while averaging 4.3 turnovers per game. Peyton Watson has struggled with his shot early into his Cavs career, although he's been terrific defensively.

We need a bigger sample size to see if Cleveland deserves to be called a true contender in the East.

The Dallas Mavericks have already picked up a pair of quality wins against the Indiana Pacers and Miami Heat while Kyrie Irving has looked good coming off a missed season due to a torn ACL. Add in Cooper Flagg continuing his ascent to superstardom and things have been overwhelmingly positive in Dallas to date.

Flagg's playmaking ability has taken a step forward and the 19-year-old currently leads the NBA in steals (3.7 per game). Irving is averaging 19.0 points on 51.2 percent shooting overall in just 27.1 minutes as the Mavs have posted an offense in the top half of the league.

Losses to good teams like the Houston Rockets and San Antonio Spurs are understandable, as the Mavericks are trying to balance winning with developing the young talent on the roster.

The Denver Nuggets are just 1-2 to begin the season, needing overtime just to take down the New Orleans Pelicans at home. A 20-point home loss to a bad Golden State Warriors team was a tough pill to swallow for a franchise that entered the season with championship aspirations.

Nikola Jokić is already beefing with the fans while his individual numbers and efficiency are all down from the previous few years. Denver's offense was the best in the NBA last year, yet has fallen all the way to 18th overall now. An already shaky defense has plummeted to No. 26 overall .

Is it too early to panic for a Nuggets team that's still above the second apron? Or has the championship window closed?

Starting this season 4-1 overall with arguably the NBA's hardest schedule, the Detroit Pistons should be very pleased with how the 2026-27 season has begun.

Wins over the Boston Celtics, Miami Heat and Philadelphia 76ers helped prove that the Pistons belong at the top of the East despite an offseason of inactivity. A lone loss to a hungry New York Knicks team was understandable.

Duncan Robinson (17.8 points per game) can't be a No. 2 offensive option for the rest of the season, however, and Ron Holland II (3.5 points on 31.6 percent shooting) is looking more and more like a bust now in Year 3.

There are certainly some question marks surrounding this roster, although Detroit should be happy with its record overall.

A 22-point opening night loss to the Los Angeles Lakers may have set the tone for the Golden State Warriors' season.

A 1-3 record to begin the year feels about right when looking up and down a roster that's missing an injured Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porziņģis and Moses Moody.

Draymond Green has made four shots in three games, ranking 14th among the Warriors' 15 players. Golden State has never relied on Green to fill up the basket, yet he now has 10 more turnovers than made shots. That's a troubling imbalance for the 36-year-old, who is averaging just 3.3 points per game.

Even Green's defense can't save the Warriors, as a 121.1 rating ranks 28th overall , barely besting the Sacramento Kings.

The return of Fred VanVleet from a torn ACL has helped stabilize a Houston Rockets offense that now ranks No. 3 overall in the NBA, fueling the team's 4-0 start. The veteran point guard has 21 total assists against just two turnovers.

Kevin Durant (23.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.5 blocks, 47.1 percent from three) continues to defy father time now at age 38. The Rockets have been hot from outside the arc (39.0 percent, fifth-best in the NBA) and rebounding remains a strong suit with the size of this frontline.

Quality wins over the San Antonio Spurs, Dallas Mavericks and Atlanta Hawks (twice) have the Rockets sitting at the top of the West.

The return of Tyrese Haliburton didn't magically make the 2-2 Indiana Pacers a contender again overnight, as a bad loss to the Milwaukee Bucks and wins over the lowly New Orleans Pelicans and Brooklyn Nets haven't inspired much confidence.

Haliburton has looked good in his return from a torn Achilles (21.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 9.5 assists, 1.3 steals), yet is now expected to miss at least two weeks with a left hamstring strain, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Obviously, the Pacers will be extremely cautious with any injury issues involving Haliburton. This group will have to prove it can stay afloat in the East without him, something they failed to do for most of last year.

The Los Angeles Clippers were always going to struggle to piece together wins this season with a retooled roster. Injuries to Brandon Ingram and Max Strus have only complicated matters.

Darius Garland looks healthy and ready to rock once again (24.0 points, 7.0 assists), yet needs to cut down on his turnovers. He's probably being asked to do too much right now, with a usage rate ( 31.3 percent ) exceeding even that of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Brunson.

The Clippers aren't going to go far with Brook Lopez as their second-leading scorer (18.0 points), although Keaton Wagler has looked promising and should take on a larger offensive role as the year progresses. A 1-2 start to the season should be considered a win.

Luka Dončić has been the best player in the NBA so far this season, leading all scorers with 36.0 points per game and guiding the Los Angeles Lakers to a 3-1 start.

Now with a roster that's been built around him, Dončić is lighting the league on fire. There's simply no guarding him when Dončić's confidence is flowing, as he only needs an inch of space to get a shot off.

Even Walker Kessler hasn't fixed a 22nd-ranked defense, although Dončić and Austin Reaves have led the second-best offense in the NBA ( 126.7 rating ) and the league's best three-point shooting attack ( 41.3 percent ).

The Lakers don't yet have a win over a team with a winning record, however, so we'll need more time to see just how good this new-look roster really is.

Just one of three teams to begin the season a perfect 4-0, the Memphis Grizzlies are the biggest surprise of the NBA season.

A healthy Ty Jerome has always been dangerous, although he's never been given this big of an offensive role before. Jerome's 29.8 points per game rank third overall in the NBA, only behind Luka Dončić and Anthony Edwards.

No. 3 overall pick Cameron Boozer hasn't shot the ball well, yet has made his impact in a number of other ways. The 19-year-old is averaging 14.8 points, 10.5 rebounds ( fifth-most in the NBA ) and 4.8 assists to begin his career. He's going to make a lot of future All-Star teams.

A fifth-ranked defense after trading away Jaren Jackson Jr. is a nice surprise, as Memphis has shocked the NBA world thus far.

The Miami Heat are finally in the win column, although a 1-4 start to the season has been a disaster of a debut for Giannis Antetokounmpo in South Beach.

Ranking in the bottom seven in the NBA in both offense and defense , Miami hasn't gotten much from its guards while Bam Adebayo averaged just 11.8 points on 16.7 percent shooting from three in his first four games.

The additions of Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. have made little impact, as neither player defends well at this stage of his career, and both have struggled to shoot from deep.

There was always going to be an adjustment period given the amount of roster sacrificed to bring in Antetokounmpo, although this is a worse start than we all predicted.

A 1-3 record to begin the season with losses to the Chicago Bulls and Washington Wizards is about what we expected for the Milwaukee Bucks.

Beyond a bad record, however, is the miserable play of Myles Turner, who's starting over Kel'el Ware in what we can assume is an attempt to increase the veteran center's trade value. Instead, Turner is averaging a career-low 7.3 points and 5.5 rebounds while shooting 36.7 percent overall.

This was never going to be an easy year for the Bucks. Milwaukee hasn't been the worst team in the NBA this year, but that distinction is certainly still in play.

A perfect 3-0 start with all three wins coming by 20 points or more had the Minnesota Timberwolves buzzing to begin the year. Even an overtime loss in Cleveland against the Cavaliers saw Anthony Edwards go for 47 points, moving him up to second overall in scoring in the NBA.

Unfortunately, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months following an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee, putting him out until around Christmas.

This doesn't mean the Wolves' season is doomed, of course. LaMelo Ball (14.8 points, 6.3 assists, 1.8 steals) has helped electrify the offense while also playing the best defense of his career. Ayo Dosunmu, Jonathan Kuminga and Terrence Shannon Jr. are all capable of stepping into bigger roles.

A plus-16.8 net rating (second in the NBA) will drop with no Edwards, although Minnesota should be thrilled by how their new healthy core looks together.

Despite being 0-3 this season, the New Orleans Pelicans are only 18th in net rating ( minus-2.4 ). That tops even some two- and three-win teams, as the Pels have kept all of their games close.

Still, a loss is a loss. Following a summer of inactivity, New Orleans opting to run back the same roster that missed the playoffs last year was a puzzling decision, one that looks even worse now.

Jeremiah Fears is struggling (8.3 points on 29.0 percent shooting) and Herb Jones has been squeezed to the back part of the rotation for some reason.

The Pelicans are a mess, but they've at least been a respectable mess.

This is the same starting five that won a championship just four months ago, right? Or do we have some sort of Monstars situation on our hands?

The New York Knicks have begun the 2026-27 season just 1-3 overall, with some of their top players struggling. Mikal Bridges looks like a shell of himself on offense (5.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 27.3 percent shooting overall) while even Jalen Brunson has struggled with his efficiency (36.6 percent shooting overall, 20.0 percent from three).

A 27th-ranked offense looks nothing like the version that finished fourth overall last year, despite the same starting five returning. The Knicks will eventually climb back above .500 and towards the top of the East, although it's been a rough start for the defending champs.

No team has been hit harder by injuries this season than the Oklahoma City Thunder. No team is better suited to handle those absences than OKC, either.

Jalen Williams is expected to miss the entire season with a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle. Cason Wallace could be out months with a torn labrum while players like Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso have also missed time due to injury.

Have we mentioned that the Thunder are a perfect 4-0 to begin the season?

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander may win MVP number three at this rate, as he's once again putting up big scoring numbers (27.3 points per game) in a role that will only increase with Williams and Wallace out.

Death. Taxes. The Orlando Magic losing key starters to injuries.

A 1-3 start to the season by Orlando can be attributed to the loss of Paolo Banchero (ankle sprain) and Jalen Suggs (bone bruise), both of whom will be out at least for a few weeks.

The Magic offense is once again offensive to watch, as a 106.5 rating ranks 26th overall in the NBA even with players like Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane suiting up in every game thus far.

Is it time to make a big move to shake up this roster? Or can a healthy Orlando team still compete in the East?

A 4-1 start for the new-look Philadelphia 76ers is about as good as anyone could have hoped for, especially with quality wins over the Cleveland Cavaliers, New York Knicks and Indiana Pacers.

A single loss to the 4-1 Detroit Pistons isn't anything for Philly to hang their heads over.

This team is still prioritizing Tyrese Maxey as the main scoring threat, as they should. His 28.8 points per game rank fourth in the NBA , while Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown are both breaking north of 20 themselves.

LeBron James appears to be adapting to his role as the fourth option on offense while serving as a playmaker and super Swiss Army knife. A fourth-ranked defense (103.3 rating) is particularly impressive, especially given the amount of offensive firepower we know this roster possesses.

The "Big 4" of Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges is off to a rough start for the 1-2 Phoenix Suns.

In their first 101 possessions together, Booker, Green, Brooks and Bridges have a net rating of minus-42.6 . Even for a relatively small sample size, this is shockingly bad.

The Suns rank dead last in the NBA in defense (124.5 rating), a mark that should (hopefully) improve whenever Mark Williams can return to the court from a torn labrum. There's talent on this roster, although the trade for Bridges looks both unnecessary and harmful to the team's ability to upgrade in the future.

Jalen Green will almost certainly have to be moved to a sixth man role or traded outright at some point. He simply doesn't fit alongside Booker and company here.

Outside of the Memphis Grizzlies, the Portland Trail Blazers have been the biggest surprise in the NBA this season.

After the first week-plus, Portland ranks:

No. 1 in assist-to-turnover ratio ( 2.24 )

No. 1 in rebound percentage ( 57.5 percent )

This has been a remarkable showing for a team that looked like it could have a real fit issue between Damian Lillard and Ja Morant, both of whom have shined in their respective roles.

Deni Avdija looks like an All-Star once again (22.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists) and Toumani Camara is 13-of-22 from deep to begin the season (59.1 percent).

If there's something more powerful than a green light for a shooter, rookie Darius Acuff Jr. certainly has it.

His 23.3 shot attempts per game are second in the NBA only to Anthony Edwards and almost as many as the next two Sacramento Kings players combined (Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis, 28.1).

However, a 34.4 percent shooting mark from the field and 20.6 percent success rate from three mean that most of these attempts are missing their target.

The 0-4 Kings are predictably horrible on defense (122.1 rating, 29th overall ) but are also dreadful on offense (105.1 rating, 28th overall ).

This is the worst team in the NBA, and it may not be close.

A 2-2 San Antonio Spurs team is tinkering with a new starting lineup that features all three of their star guards, making sure everyone is at least somewhat happy.

The results have been solid so far, with Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama registering a net rating of plus-9.2 together (88 total possessions).

Wembanyama ranks just 30th overall in scoring this season (22.3 points per game) and is making 21.1 percent of his threes, essentially bailing the defense out whenever he hoists up an outside shot.

This doesn't look like the well-oiled machine that tore through the Western Conference last spring, but the Spurs have still played well, losing only to the red-hot Oklahoma City Thunder and Houston Rockets.

The Toronto Raptors look like a dark horse to come out of the Eastern Conference thanks to the addition of Kawhi Leonard and an incredible defense, but it's still too early to tell how good they are.

Wins against the lowly Chicago Bulls and Washington Wizards were expected, although a 23-point loss to a formidable Minnesota Timberwolves team was a disappointment. The Raptors do own the NBA's best defense right now (97.8 rating), a figure that may climb now with the latest Leonard news.

The seven-time All-Star is expected to miss a period of weeks due to swelling in his left knee, per ESPN's Shams Charania , meaning Leonard made it exactly two regular season games before having to miss time.

There's enough talent on this Raptors team to win without him, although this may not be the elite East team we thought that it could be with Leonard.

Expectations were beginning to shift for a Utah Jazz team that's finally fielding a competitive NBA roster.

A 1-3 start to the season has been a disappointment, especially considering Utah's lone win came against the 0-3 New Orleans Pelicans (by a single point, no less).

The Jazz began the season without Jusuf Nurkić due to a foot injury, and now Jaren Jackson Jr. is expected to be sidelined for six to eight weeks with a torn MCL in his right knee.

No 2. overall pick Darryn Peterson is going to have to adjust quickly following a slow start (11.5 points on 36.0 percent shooting overall), as the team will need his scoring with so many frontcourt bodies now out.

A 2-2 record with a net rating of exactly 0.0 is about as average as it gets, although the Washington Wizards deserve a slight bump up from a C grade here.

No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa did not play in the Wizards' first four games but should make his NBA debut soon. Trae Young currently leads the league in assists (11.0) and Anthony Davis (22.8 points, 9.3 rebounds) has looked dominant at times.

We know the injury bug will hit Davis at some point, so staying at a .500 pace to begin the season is a good start for a Wizards team desperate to return to relevancy.
