articles.title: Lakers vs. Clippers Box Score Stats, Highlights for Austin Reaves, Top Players With Luka, Ingram Out
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers cruised past the Los Angeles Clippers 103-87 on Wednesday night to make it four wins from five to open the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers cruised past the Los Angeles Clippers 103-87 on Wednesday night to make it four wins from five to open the 2026-27 NBA season.

Six-time All-Star Luka Dončić was sidelined due to back tightness. That allowed some of the Lakers' offseason additions to shine. Quentin Grimes led the team in scoring with 23 points.

Grimes' four steals were an example of why the Lakers signed him in the first place.

Lakers fans got the full Collin Sexton experience as the veteran guard poured in 21 points and lived up to his Young Bull nickname on defense.

In general, the game couldn't have gone much better for JJ Redick's squad.

Dončić is inevitably going to miss a few more games through rest or a minor injury here and there. He has never logged more than 72 appearances in a season. The supporting cast will have to step up when he's not available, and that's what happened on Wednesday night.

The performance of No. 5 overall pick Keaton Wagler at least served as a silver lining for the Clippers. He had 21 points and four rebounds off the bench. One of his four made field goals was a buzzer-beater at the end of the third.

Wagler's 12 free-throw attempts illustrated how aggressive he was in getting to the basket.

The Clippers could claim to having the single biggest highlight as well. Forward Isaiah Jackson reached back to collect a lob from Darius Garland and finish an alley-oop in the third.

The Lakers will head north to face off with the Golden State Warriors on Friday with aims of repeating their 22-point victory on opening night.

The Clippers will try to stop their three-game losing skid when they hit the road against the Minnesota Timberwolves, who will be without Anthony Edwards, on Friday.

articles.title: 2027 Men's NCAA Tournament Preseason Bracket Projections
articles.summary: Ready, eligible for a fifth year or not, the return of men's college basketball is just around the corner.
articles.body:
Ready, eligible for a fifth year or not, the return of men's college basketball is just around the corner.

Notre Dame and Villanova will square off in Rome on Sunday morning, followed about 12 hours later by the Field of 68's Opening Day 24-hour marathon.

In other words, it's time to start resting up for that beginning of the twisting, winding, loop-de-looping journey to crowning the 2027 national champion.

We cannot allow the season to begin without a projected bracket, though.

I won't lie to you, fine folks: As has been my tradition over the past six years, most of the research that went into the seeding for this bracket involved aggregating team rankings published by others.

While it's not exactly an average of team rankings from KenPom , BartTorvik , EvanMiya , Haslametrics , Matt Norlander's Top 100 And 1 for CBS Sports and Kevin Sweeney's ranking of all 365 teams for Sports Illustrated , the average of those six was our starting point, from which manual adjustments were made here and there.

On top of that, the projected automatic bid for each of the 32 conferences is simply the team that was picked to win the league in the respective preseason media polls. (Work smarter, not harder.)

We all know the goal of preseason bracket projections isn't to be as accurate as possible, though. (Especially this year.) It's just a fun way to get hyped for the next five months, while maybe giving a few teams some bulletin-board material to carry as a chip on their shoulder.

So, let's dive into this new 76-team world with some thoughts on the biggest wild cards in each of the major conferences and a preposterously early Cinderella pick.

Please forgive any possible first-round pairings that are rematches of scheduled nonconference games. I won't start accounting for that until later, after we've got this new 76-team format down to something resembling a science.

10 Words on Each of the 10 'Bubbliest' Teams

Fifth-to-Last In : Maryland Terrapins—If Buzz Williams gets D.J. Wagner to shine, look out.

Fourth-to-Last In : Utah State Aggies—MWC has to get two bids with 76 teams, right?

Third-to-Last In : Providence Friars—Bryan Hodgson's meteoric rise continues, getting the Friars dancing again.

Second-to-Last In : Saint Louis Billikens—If Robbie Avila actually plays, this is way too low.

Last Team In : LSU Tigers—If you have any clue where they belong, do tell.

First Team Out : San Diego State Aztecs—Average ranking of 62.7 feels like a pretty big oversight.

Second Team Out : NC State Wolfpack—A No. 11 seed for fourth time in five years?

Third Team Out : Ole Miss Rebels—Could bounce back in big way from 20 loss campaign.

Fourth Team Out : TCU Horned Frogs—Season could hinge on up-transfers Gavin Sykes and Trent Lincoln.

Fifth Team Out : Minnesota Golden Gophers—Year No. 2 under Niko Medved could be a breakthrough.

6 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 1. Duke, 12. Louisville, 14. Virginia, 21. Miami (FL), 35. North Carolina, 43. Clemson

Also Considered: NC State, Virginia Tech, Florida State, SMU

Biggest Wild Card: The Michael Malone Experiment at North Carolina

Over the past two decades, we've lost Billy Donovan, Brad Stevens, Fred Hoiberg (temporarily), John Beilein and now Dusty May to the NBA.

But who knew that was still a two-way street?

North Carolina hiring Michael Malone to replace Hubert Davis as head coach was a colossal stunner when it was announced during Final Four weekend, but he brings quite a coaching pedigree with him to Chapel Hill. The Denver Nuggets made the playoffs in each of his final seven seasons coaching there, including winning a title in 2023.

Nikola Jokic isn't walking through that door, though, and the Tar Heels have had to replace eight of their nine leading scorers from last season—stretch-4 Jarin Stevenson the lone returnee of the bunch.

As a result, Malone has rebuilt this roster via a little bit of every avenue possible.

Neo Avdalas (Virginia Tech) and Matt Able (NC State) were key players elsewhere in the ACC last season, but they figure to start alongside FDU/Utah transfer Terrence Brown in North Carolina's backcourt.

Freshman Sayon Keita and Maximo Adams will feature prominently in the frontcourt mix. The former is 7'1" with a knack for rejections (five blocks in the exhibition game vs. Indiana). The latter was a McDonald's All-American who may well be the ACC's sixth man of the year if he's not starting.

And watch out for 6'11" international prospect Alex Samodurov. Like Avdalas, Samodurov has been playing professionally in Greece for about half a decade at this point. If he hits the ground running, UNC's ceiling could be the roof.

9 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 3. Arizona, 5. Houston, 8. Kansas, 10. Iowa State, 18. Texas Tech, 27. BYU, 30. Baylor, 38. Cincinnati, 45. West Virginia

Also Considered: TCU, Oklahoma State, UCF

Biggest Wild Card: Kansas' Three-Headed Eligibility Battle

In Tre White, Melvin Council Jr. and Trey Kaufman-Renn, Bill Self has a trio of veterans who could lead Kansas to the Final Four.

If they're allowed to play at all, that is.

White and Council were two of the four Jayhawks who scored at least 400 points last season, while TKR was racking up more than 500 points and 300 rebounds at Purdue. And they have all sued for one more year of eligibility.

At the moment, all three are considered eligible. TKR did not play in the exhibition game against Duke on Sunday, but did play in the previous one against Louisville. White and Council combined to play 55 minutes against the Blue Devils.

If all three play all season alongside 5-star freshmen Tyran Stokes and Taylen Kinney, Kansas might be the best team in the country. We'll see about the frontcourt, but if either Keanu Dawes (from Utah) or Christian Reeves (from College of Charleston) emerges as a legitimate 5, that team would be a certified problem.

Without White, Council and Kaufman-Renn, you almost had to squint to see a single-digit seed in this roster's future, even with Stokes' potential to be a superstar.

The Jayhawks are hardly alone in having an on-court outlook shaped by decisions in a different kind of court. But they might have the largest gap between their ceiling and their floor, depending on how those eligibility cases ultimately play out.

6 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 6. Connecticut, 17. St. John's, 28. Villanova, 33. Marquette, 44. Creighton, 49. Providence

Also Considered: Xavier, DePaul, Seton Hall

Biggest Wild Card: Can Marquette Bounce All the Way Back?

On the one hand, Marquette has a total of nine players back from last season, including four crucial returnees in Nigel James Jr., Royce Parham, Adrien Stevens and Caedin Hamilton. (Though, Hamilton is recovering from a torn calf and could miss the entirety of nonconference play.) Each one started at least 17 games in 2025-26, and James, in particular, should be one of the best players in the Big East this year after averaging 16 points and five assists per game as a freshman.

On the other hand, last season was a disaster for Marquette, suffering at least 20 losses for just the second time in program history. (The other happened all the way back in 1963-64.)

Roster retention is usually a wonderful thing.

Shaka Smart did pick up a pair of crucial transfers in Sananda Fru (Louisville) and Nolan Minessale (St. Thomas), as well as a freshman in Alex Egbuonu who could play a huge role immediately. That trio of newbies combined for 31 points in Marquette's exhibition victory over Michigan State on Sunday, so it's much more than just the returnees.

Smart has coached his way back from worse, too. In his second season at Texas, the Longhorns went 11-22. But they were back in the NCAA tournament the following year. He also had the Golden Eagles in the dance as a single-digit seed in each of his first four years on the job, and there are high hopes he can do so again in year No. 6.

12 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 4. Illinois, 7. Michigan State, 13. Michigan, 20. Nebraska, 23. UCLA, 25. Purdue, 26. Ohio State, 36. USC, 37. Indiana, 39. Wisconsin, 41. Iowa, 47. Maryland

Biggest Wild Card: How Will the Reigning National Champions Fare?

The entire landscape of college basketball has changed in the not-even-seven months since Michigan cut down the nets at Lucas Oil Stadium.

Where do the new-look Wolverines fit into the mix?

Usually, the reigning champ is a shoo-in for a top 10 ranking in the subsequent preseason AP poll.

But after losing Yaxel Lendeborg, Aday Mara and Morez Johnson Jr. as lottery picks, losing head coach Dusty May to the Dallas Mavericks and losing highly touted freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. to a torn ACL suffered in August, the Wolverines landed at No. 16 in the AP poll and No. 20 in the Coaches poll.

They do have Elliot Cadeau, Trey McKenney and Roddy Gayle Jr. back, so the backcourt is going to look pretty familiar.

This frontcourt is mighty questionable, though, with transfers Moustapha Thiam (Cincinnati) and J.P. Estrella (Tennessee) the only sure things they've got in the paint. If either one ends up being less productive than he was in 2025-26, that could spell disaster.

Early returns from the exhibition games suggest this team is going to live and die by the three even more so than they ever did under John Beilein. At any rate, the long ball accounted for 66 percent of their field-goal attempts in the 17-point loss to Houston, so they better make them at a good clip.

13 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 2. Florida, 11. Texas, 15. Alabama, 16. Tennessee, 19. Arkansas, 22. Vanderbilt, 24. Kentucky, 29. Auburn, 31. Texas A&M, 32. Missouri, 34. Oklahoma, 40. Georgia, 51. LSU

Biggest Wild Card: The Curious Case of LSU's Roster

Throw it at the wall and see what sticks.

For LSU, roster building has also meant waiting to see what the courts allow.

Will Wade assembled a roster featuring several players whose availability depended on eligibility rulings , leaving the Tigers with considerable uncertainty heading into the season.

For a while, it was hard to know what that roster would actually look like.

As recently as October 8—the morning of their first exhibition game against McNeese— they had just four players publicly listed on their official roster. And in that game that they barely won, their starting five played darn near every minute, because what other choice did they have?

Within the subsequent 16 days, Skyy Clark, Saliou Niang and Brice Dessert were all cleared , at least temporarily. Meanwhile, RJ Luis Jr.'s lawyers are asking a Louisiana judge to block the SEC from punishing LSU if the Tigers add him to their roster. The former St. John's guard entered the 2025 NBA draft and later briefly signed with two NBA teams without appearing in an NBA game.

He secured a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in October, but his availability remains disputed.

With those first three added to the mix, though, they had a much more legitimate, eight-man rotation for their Oct. 24 exhibition against Florida State. They now have a 14-man roster on their official website .

But as lawsuits continue to play out around the country, we're all kind of bracing for the inevitability of fluctuating roster situations well beyond the normal injury-based wear and tear—and expecting LSU to be more susceptible to it than most.

Sounds as plausible as anything for LSU.

Mid-Majors Summary (A10, AAC, MVC, MWC, P12, WCC)

9 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 9. Gonzaga, 42. VCU, 46. Grand Canyon, 48. Utah State, 50. Saint Louis, 53. New Mexico, 54. Wichita State, 55. Santa Clara, 56. Murray State

Also Considered: San Diego State, George Mason, Boise State, Dayton, Nevada, Saint Mary's

Biggest Wild Card: Robbie Avila back at Saint Louis?

We thought we had seen the last of Robbie "Cream Abdul-Jabbar" Avila when Saint Louis lost to Michigan in the second round of the most recent NCAA tournament.

But last week, a judge granted Avila a temporary restraining order allowing him to return to Saint Louis while his eligibility challenge continues. He has already been practicing with the team and could play in Monday's season opener against Lehigh.

Even without him, the Billikens looked like a potential tournament team.

Josh Schertz managed to retain five of his seven leading scorers, including one of the best three-point shooters in the nation in Trey Green. He and Kellen Thames were both named to the A-10 preseason all-conference first team, with Amari McCottry and Ishan Sharma cracking second and third team, respectively.

Schertz also added a quality freshman in point guard Jermel Thomas and a trio of high-major transfers in Alon Michaeli (Colorado), Elijah Strong (South Carolina) and Sheek Pearson (Marquette). [The latter redshirted for the Golden Eagles, but was a 4-star recruit who could make a major impact in the SLU frontcourt.]

Throw Avila and his 1,990 career points back into the calculus, though, and the Billikens become much more than just a co-favorite (along with VCU) to win the A-10. They could be a legitimate top 25 team and a candidate to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time since 1957—when there only were 23 teams in the dance and they got a bye to the regional semis.

As is, they are narrowly in our projected field, for quite the acronym showdown of a play-in game between SLU and LSU. But this is the mid-major we're most looking forward to watching through the first month of the season. (Doesn't hurt that the Billikens will face Missouri, Grand Canyon, Saint Mary's and High Point within their first six games.)

21 Teams in the Projected Field (by Overall Seed): 52. High Point, 57. UNC Wilmington, 58. McNeese, 59. UC Irvine, 60. Western Kentucky, 61. Miami (OH), 62. Penn, 63. Montana State, 64. Furman, 65. Wright State, 66. North Dakota State, 67. Central Arkansas, 68. Queens, 69. Howard, 70. Vermont, 71. Arkansas State, 72. Merrimack, 73. American, 74. Tennessee State, 75. Bethune Cookman, 76. LIU

Biggest Wild Card: Is UNC Wilmington this year's Miami (OH)?

UNC Wilmington has won exactly 27 games in each of the past two seasons. It's a mark that the Seahawks also reached in 2021-22. They've won at least 21 games in five straight years.

And with nary a game on their schedule against a team in the KenPom top 120, we're already putting the Seahawks on irresponsibly early "undefeated watch."

Takayo Siddle has had to replace an awful lot of last year's squad. In fact, of the six leading scorers from 2025-26, only big man Patrick Wessler returns for UNCW.

He was the no-brainer pick for preseason CAA Player of the Year, though, while transfers CJ Luster II, William Kermoury and Xavier Brown figure to become major cogs in this team's primary seven-man rotation.

Also from this tier, High Point has a good chance at another special season.

The Panthers have gone 87-20 over the past three years, and they somehow found another year of eligibility for Cam'Ron Fletcher, who played his first season at Kentucky way back in 2020-21. He and fellow three-time transfers Jason Rivera-Torres and Curtis Williams Jr. will lead the way, alongside South Florida transfer point guard CJ Brown.

High Point won't be surprising anyone, though. The Panthers might even have some at-large potential if they happen to slip up in the Big South tournament.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Reacts to Anthony Edwards' Injury in Video, Talks Wolves Star's Recovery Timeline
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry offered some advice to Anthony Edwards with the Minnesota Timberwolves guard sidelined for a stretch.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry offered some advice to Anthony Edwards with the Minnesota Timberwolves guard sidelined for a stretch.

Edwards will miss multiple weeks due to a knee injury. After Golden State's 119-114 win over Minnesota on Wednesday, Curry told reporters he reached out to the four-time All-Star after they've built a rapport through the U.S. national team.

"I know he's gone through some stuff with the knee, but you just gotta have to do what you can with the rehab," he said. "Attack it the same way you do getting ready for games."

Ant's Injury Doesn't Worry Wolves' President

Curry battled ankle trouble early in his career and there were some fears it could be a problem that dogged him for years to come. That didn't prove to be the case, though injuries have limited the two-time MVP a bit as he got into his 30s.

The 2019-20 was a nadir on that front as Curry played just five games after breaking his left hand.

The prognosis for Edwards could be much worse. Barring any setbacks, he's going to return at some point this season.

But watching your team from afar for multiple months is always a frustrating experience, especially when you have championship aspirations.

Unfortunately for Edwards, there's no way to speed up the recovery process. That's often how those costly setbacks occur.

The Warriors and Timberwolves will cross paths again on Dec. 27. Perhaps Edwards will be healthy for Minnesota's next meeting with Curry.

articles.title: Mirotic es baja para varias semanas en el Valencia Básket
articles.standfirst: Se pierde, para empezar, el partido de mañana en el Palau ante el Barça tras sufrir una lesión en el aductor de su pierna izquierda
articles.summary: Se pierde, para empezar, el partido de mañana en el Palau ante el Barça tras sufrir una lesión en el aductor de su pierna izquierda
articles.body: El ala-pívot del Valencia Basket Nikola Mirotic será baja los próximos partidos tras haber sufrido una lesión muscular en el encuentro que enfrentó a su equipo y al Fenerbahce el pasado martes en la Euroliga y no estará por tanto en el duelo en la pista del Barça en esta competición este viernes. El técnico del equipo valenciano, Xavi Albert, aseguró este jueves que no espera poder contar con el jugador nacido en Montenegro antes de dos semanas, un plazo parecido al que le da para reaparecer a Nate Reuvers, que se ha perdido los últimos dos partidos por una lesión en un pie. Mirotic sufrió un pinchazo en la pierna izquierda en el duelo ante el equipo otomano y aunque intentó volver a jugar finalmente no pudo acabar el choque. Las pruebas de imagen a las que ha sido sometido el jugador han confirmado que sufre una lesión muscular en el aductor de la pierna izquierda y el Valencia confirmó su baja "para los próximos compromisos" a la espera de que su evolución le permita incorporarse a los entrenamientos

articles.title: Steve Kerr Calls Out NBA Players for Flopping in Video, 'We Should Be the No Bulls--t Association'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr wants to see the NBA crack down harder on players flopping.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr wants to see the NBA crack down harder on players flopping.

Speaking to reporters prior to Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves, Kerr said "we should be the No Bulls--t Association" in speaking about flopping and how it gets called by the officials.

"Like, every bit of bulls--t that the players try to pull, we should just say, 'No, no. We're not doing that.' And it's a better game when guys aren't flopping, guys aren't grabbing each other, hooking each other, running into screens and looking like they got hit by a car," Kerr added. "It's just a better game when the officials have the ability to just say, 'No. We're not buying into that.' And I feel like we are constantly, as a league, sort of behind the players. The players are grifting and we're chasing them and we're never getting ahead of it. And that's my biggest issue."

The flopping question came up after Tuesday's game between the Portland Trail Blazers and Los Angeles Lakers. There was a two-minute sequence in the fourth quarter when officials called technical fouls on Ja Morant, Toumani Camara and Ziaire Williams for flopping on defense.

Prior to the start of the regular season, the NBA unveiled the main points of emphasis it was focusing on for players, coaches and referees. One of the points on the list was on "exaggerated and theatrical" movements aimed at getting a favorable call.

Kerr also revealed he sent clips to the NBA office early in the season about various calls, but he declined to publicly comment on what his conversations with league officials entailed.

One thing Kerr made sure to emphasize was he thinks "our officials do a great job" overall and everyone needs "to stay ahead of all the player grifting."

There were no such technical-foul issues between the Warriors and Timberwolves on Wednesday night. Golden State left the Target Center with a 119-114 victory thanks to 44 points from Stephen Curry and a near-double-double from Yaxel Lendeborg with 26 points and nine rebounds.

The Warriors have won back-to-back games after their 0-3 start. They will look to get back to the .500 mark on Friday when they host the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Bulls Rookie Caleb Wilson Makes Honest Admission After Loss To Knicks
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls dropped their third straight game on Wednesday, October 28, losing to the New York Knicks 133-127.Once again, star rookie Caleb Wilson impr...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls dropped their third straight game on Wednesday, October 28, losing to the New York Knicks 133-127.

Once again, star rookie Caleb Wilson impressed, putting up 20 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists, and two steals. However, Wilson's efficiency will be something he wants to work on after going 7-of-18 from the field, including 3-of-8 from deep.

Still, for Wilson, this was likely a 'Welcome to the NBA' moment, as he faced off against the reigning NBA Champions. After the game, Wilson spoke glowingly about the talent the Knicks have at their disposal.

"Jalen Brunson cold," Wilson admitted. "Then KAT is just––he's huge, he's huge, he just makes the right decision, can shoot, trail threes, just plays the basketball really well. Honestly, they're just a good team. OG's really good too, really physical, hard to go against, hard to score against, they just have a really well-rounded team."

"Even Jordan Clarkson came the bench and finished it. He played really well. We get to play them again next week at their place. We'll learn from this and hopefully we can go out there and get a win."

Wilson is only five games into his NBA career. As such, he will have many more of these moments as he continues to face off against the best players in the world.

Bulls' Norman Powell Continues To Impress

Despite Chicago slumping to its fourth loss this season, and third in a row, Norman Powell was impressive once again. The Bulls' marquee free-agent addition dropped 30 points on the Knicks, along with grabbing 2 boards and dishing out 2 assists.

Overall, Powell shot 44.4% from the three-point range on 4-of-9 shooting. He was also successful elsewhere on the floor, going 10-of-15 from the field in total. If he continues to play at this level, Chicago will have a strong trade chip to dangle once we get closer to the trade deadline.

In his first five games for the Bulls, Powell is averaging 21.6 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists, shooting 36.6% from deep.

Tiago Splitter Pleased With Bulls Level of Fight

Chicago may have lost against the Knicks, but that doesn't mean there weren't signs of improvement from the young and rebuilding roster.

During his postgame news conference, head coach Tiago Splitter praised his team's level of competitiveness and fight.

"We were focused for a longer period of time throughout the game, which is good, but the game still has 48 minutes," Splitter said, via Roundtable. "That last quarter tonight wasn't good enough. Of course, they have great players… That's why they won the championship. But I think we competed for the most part. We got better tonight."

Bulls fans knew this season was going to be a rollercoaster coming into the season. Rebuilding teams need time for internal development to take place, and for the coaching to start paying dividends.

However, playing hard is totally within the team's control, and against the Knicks, Chicago showed signs that it will be a tough out for any team as we get deeper and deeper into the season.

articles.title: NBA injury worries continue to mount as Jalen Williams, Anthony Edwards and other key players add to a troubling league-wide trend
articles.summary: One week into the 2026-27 season, the NBA injury report is hard to read without wincing.
articles.body: One week into the 2026-27 season, the NBA injury report is hard to read without wincing. Jalen Williams is out with a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle. Anthony Edwards is headed for knee surgery. A long list of starters from Orlando to Utah has joined them on the sideline, and one count puts about 15 percent of the league on the injured or ill list in a single day. Rotations are breaking before they have been built. Nobody can say why, and the theories keep piling up.What has happened to NBA stars in the first week of the season?Jalen Williams had a very concerning injury. The Thunder star went down in the third game with a fractured fibula and a dislocated left ankle, a gruesome injury that drew Gordon Hayward comparisons. Oklahoma City will re-evaluate him before the regular season ends, but a return this year is a long shot. He had already missed most of last season.Cason Wallace left the same game. The $139 million Thunder starter has a torn labrum in his left shoulder, needs surgery, and is likely done for most of the year, if not all of it.Anthony Edwards is next. The Minnesota star has a right knee problem that needs an arthroscopic procedure. Two months away would bring him back close to the new year.Now, it is quite hard to look at where the injuries landed and a pattern shows up. Teams are losing players in pairs. Oklahoma City lost Williams and Wallace in one game. Utah lost Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen in another. Orlando is missing Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs at once. A coach can plan for one hole. Two starters gone in the first week leaves no time to adjust.Not every case is grim. Several players are expected back in about two weeks. The season-ending list is shorter, but it already has Williams, Wallace and Ben Simmons on it.Which NBA players are injured right now?A lot. Apart from Edwards, who is set to sit out for at least two months and Thunder’s Williams with season ending injury, there are many players already in the concerning zone. On top of that, Kristaps Porziņģis’ potential Warriors return is slim to none and he is is out indefinitely after experiencing recurring symptoms of Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), a chronic condition that affects heart rate regulation and can cause dizziness and severe fatigue.Tyrese Haliburton, PacersTyrese Haliburton came back from the Achilles rupture he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals against Oklahoma City. He lasted four games. The left hamstring strain is listed as week-to-week, and Rick Carlisle said he doesn’t think “it’s realistic that he would play before then,” with two weeks as the marker.Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs, MagicBanchero went down hard on his right ankle in the second game. The low-grade high ankle sprain is worth four to six weeks. He had 35 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds in the opener, a loss to the Hawks. Sean Sweeney won his first game as coach without him, against the Knicks.Suggs got hurt in that win with no contact, which always looks bad. The result is a right knee bone bruise and a re-check in two weeks. Jase Richardson and Anthony Black get the extra minutes.Kawhi Leonard, RaptorsKawhi Leonard’s return to Toronto has stalled on left knee swelling. ESPN’s Shams Charania reported he will miss a period of weeks, though the MRI showed no structural damage. Leonard said he is focused on getting back to full strength. His next check is in about a week.Jaren Jackson Jr., JazzJackson has a torn MCL and a six-week re-evaluation. He played only three games for Utah after Memphis traded him at last season’s deadline, so his time with the Jazz has barely started. Markkanen has a right wrist sprain and is day-to-day.Jalen Duren, PistonsJalen Duren hurt his right hamstring in the second game, a few months after a tense restricted free agency with Detroit. He is out about two weeks. The Pistons still beat the 76ers without him and Ausar Thompson.Ben Simmons, KingsSimmons tore his Achilles just before his return and is out for the season. Sacramento signed him to a one-year deal and sits at 0-4, so his next move comes in the summer.Other names on the reportThe Clippers are without Brandon Ingram (partially torn Achilles) and Max Strus (plantar fascia tear). Charlotte has Kon Knueppel and Coby White out. Alex Caruso, Ivica Zubac, Tobias Harris, Cameron Johnson, Nic Claxton, Mark Williams and Jusuf Nurkic are all dealing with injuries. Kristaps Porzingis is away from Golden State with an illness. Philadelphia’s Ariel Hukporti has a torn Achilles. And they are not all.Why are NBA injuries a big concern for the league?Start with the raw count. Keerthika Uthayakumar, formerly of TSN, posted that “79 players are listed with an injury or illness” on Wednesday’s afternoon report, about 15 percent of the league. The Kings, Blazers and Grizzlies had not reported yet. Add them and the number is 85.Load management explains part of it. Stars sit to protect their bodies, and fans have learned to live with it. But a list this long goes past rest days. A fractured fibula, a torn MCL and two torn Achilles tendons are not maintenance.The cause is still a guess. The packed schedule, faster pace, players adding muscle, shoes, and years of high-mileage youth basketball, AAU included, have all been named. A mix of several is the likeliest answer. Some fans want a shorter regular season. Traditionalists want no part of it.Teams already feel it. Oklahoma City is down two starters for most of the year, and Sacramento is 0-4 without Simmons. The league also has Edwards, Williams, Haliburton, Banchero and Duren all out at once, which thins out its early-season star power.Leonard is re-evaluated in about a week. Suggs, Haliburton and Duren all point toward returns in roughly two weeks. Edwards is the long wait, with the new year as the target. It appears that the NBA needs a cautious approach to manage injuries, as there is the whole season ahead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Angel Reese Has ‘No Doubt’ Atlanta Dream Can Force A Game 7 In WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are hoping to force a Game 7 in the ongoing WNBA Finals. Right now, […]
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are hoping to force a Game 7 in the ongoing WNBA Finals. Right now, the Georgia-based team is down 3-2 in a best-of-seven series against the newly formed Golden State Valkyries. Their next contest is October 29 at 12:30 PM ET at State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta. Before the game, several players, including Reese, Rhyne Howard, and veteran DeWanna Bonner, discussed their mindset going into the contest and vowed to fight with everything they had.

DeWanna Bonner Wants To See Her Atlanta Dream Teammates Get Back To Playing With Joy

The 2026 WNBA Finals have been quite a battle. The series opened in San Francisco at the Chase Center, where the Valks stole Game 1 by four points. The Dream punched back days later, winning Games 2 and 3.

The Valkyries returned in Game 4 with a vengeance, limiting Reese to 2-of-12 shooting, disrupting the Dream's rhythm, and stealing a road win.

Now, with their season on the line, the Dream are fighting to erase their 3-2 deficit with a stellar performance on Thursday, October 29, at State Farm Arena. If they win, the Finals return to San Francisco on October 31 for a winner-take-all celebration.

Before that, though, the Dream are focused on getting back to themselves. DeWanna Bonner told ESPN that she wants to see her teammates play with joy again.

"I feel like the last couple games, we just haven't been ourselves, and we know that," she said. "You haven't seen us smile. You haven't seen us enjoying [each other], and that's how we play."

She added, "Once you get to that moment and you get inside your head and you lose the joy of the game, it's really hard. You're playing against yourself, and you playing against the Golden State team. You can't do that."

Angel Reese Had 'Uncomfortable' Conversations About Performance With Teammates

With everything on the line in Game 6, the Dream are hoping to come out swinging at State Farm Arena.

Before that, though, Reese told the media the team needed to have "uncomfortable conversations" with each other about their performance. That talk, however, has only motivated everyone further, Reese said, adding that the team is "in a great mind space right now."

"We have no doubt," Reese said about the upcoming test. "I have no doubt that this team will come back and fight back and win this Game 6 and then move on from it."

Reese said her mind has been on the upcoming matchup since earlier this week, stating that she's been itching to get back on the hardwood.

"Just having a mindset of leaving it all out there," she said. "You're going to have to peel me off the court. I want to be so d-mn tired. I want to just be able to give everything."

The Atlanta Dream Still Believe In Themselves To Get The Job Done

It's not like the Dream aren't used to adversity. They've been battle-tested all season and through the WNBA Playoffs, defeating the Washington Mystics and the New York Liberty. They're holding on to that feeling, said Bonner.

"Our confidence is still high," she said. "There's no reason to lose confidence." Of course, Bonner has been here before, playing 17 seasons in the WNBA and winning two championships. Last year, her Phoenix Mercury made it to the finals before being swept by the Las Vegas Aces.

"We're down one game in this. We get [Game 6], and it's a series all over again," Bonner added.

Rhyne Howard Breaks Her Silence On The Dream's 3-2 Deficit

Bonner and Reese aren't alone in their feelings, according to ESPN. Rhyne Howard told the media she felt the same way about herself and her teammates.

"We don't want to just be like the world is ending because our backs are against the wall," she said. "We had them against the wall [after Game 3] and they showed up and they punched. So I think it's just our turn to come out and do the same thing."

As the series continues to play out, fans will also be watching to see how the referees handle calls. According to a previous report from The Blast , Reese and her head coach, Karl Smesko, criticized the WNBA's officials for inconsistent calls.

"I mean, a lot of us are getting fouled, and they're not calling it, or we're talking to the [referee] after, and they're saying, 'Oh, we'll get you next time.' So, it is a little frustrating, especially in the moment of it," Reese said.

In Game 5, Valkyries player Veronica Burton was allowed to keep playing after committing a hard foul to Dream player Allisha Gray's face. Unfortunately, Dream had already used their coach's challenge earlier in the contest, so they couldn't review the call for a potential upgrade to a Flagrant 1 or 2.

"But honestly, for my teammates, when they're getting slapped to the ground or goggles knocked off, like it is frustrating and trying to keep them in and keep them confident. But yeah, we'll figure it out. We're gonna have to just continue to push through the physicality, and hopefully, it goes our way next game," Reese added.

articles.title: The best players in the short history of the NBA Cup
articles.summary: HoopsHype ranks the best players in the short history of the NBA Cup, a list featuring Giannis Antetokounmpo, Jalen Brunson and Luka Doncic.
articles.body:
The NBA Cup, originally known as the In-Season Tournament, has been around for three years now, and although fans weren't originally sold on the idea, it has proven to be an entertaining, high-level competition, giving the early-season doldrums some higher stakes.

Some of the best players in history have won NBA Cup MVP awards so far, giving the accolade prestige, and the competition has even proven to be a spoiler of how the NBA playoffs would eventually go, particularly last year when the NBA Cup championship game (and result) mirrored the 2026 Finals.

With the competition set to start its fourth installment on Friday, we're going to rank the Top 10 players in NBA Cup history. Check out the results below.

Stats: 30.2 ppg, 10.1 rpg, 7.7 apg, 1.5 spg, 1.7 bpg, 64.6 FG%, 31.9 3P%

Accolades : One NBA Cup title, one NBA Cup MVP, two All-Tournament Team selections

One of three NBA Cup MVPs, former Milwaukee Bucks star Giannis Antetokounmpo really seems to wake up for this event, despite the fact that many fans still don't seem all that into it. Antetokounmpo led the Bucks to the second NBA Cup championship ever, and the first when it was named the NBA Cup and not just the In-Season Tournament. The Greek Freak was also named NBA Cup MVP that year, a well-earned honor that was capped by his performance in the final, a 97-81 Bucks win over the eventual NBA champion Oklahoma City Thunder . Antetokounmpo went off for 26 points, 19 rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and three blocks on 10-of-19 shooting in the win, dominating an elite Thunder squad on both ends of the floor. All in all, Antetokounmpo deserves kudos for stepping up in the NBA Cup, giving the event more validity at a time when many fans questioned its existence.

Stats: 31.4 ppg, 4.8 rpg, 5.8 apg, 2.4 spg, 0.8 bpg, 54.4 FG%, 37.4 3P%

Accolades : Two All-Tournament Team selections

Although he hasn't won an NBA Cup to this point, purely looking at the raw stats, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander makes a strong case to be the competition's best player ever. The Canadian superstar ranks second all-time in points per game in the NBA Cup, and first in steals per contest (among players who have participated in the event all three years). The Thunder have reached at least the semifinal in each of the last two years of the NBA Cup, getting to the final in 2024-25, where they fell in the championship game against Antetokounmpo and the Bucks. To get to the 2025 final against Milwaukee, Oklahoma City had to get past the Houston Rockets. Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder to do just that, dominating Houston to the tune of 32 points, eight rebounds, six assists, five steals and one block to give the Thunder a shot at the trophy in 2025.

Stats: 32.8 ppg, 7.8 rpg, 7.3 apg, 1.6 spg, 0.5 bpg, 50.1 FG%, 43.4 3P%

Accolades : One All-Tournament Team selection

Slovenian star Luka Doncic leads the NBA Cup in points per game, which was enough for us to rank him third in this exercise despite never advancing past the quarterfinal stage. Doncic continued his on-court statistical dominance in the In-Season Tournament and NBA Cup, hitting ridiculously tough shots from all over the floor in the event, while rebounding and playmaking at a high level and knocking down an impressive 43-plus percent of his three-point attempts. Most recently, Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers fell in the NBA Cup quarterfinals to the eventual NBA Cup finalist Spurs, 132-119, but the six-time All-Star went down swinging, going off for 35 points, five rebounds, eight assists and one steal in the losing effort.

Stats: 28.6 ppg, 3.4 rpg, 5.8 apg, 0.6 spg, 0.3 bpg, 50.9 FG%, 39.6 3P%

Accolades : One NBA Cup title, one NBA Cup MVP, one All-Tournament Team selection

In what proved to be a preview of the NBA Finals, Jalen Brunson led the New York Knicks to an NBA Cup championship in 2025-26, even doing so against the same team New York would take down in the Finals: San Antonio. Brunson earned NBA Cup MVP honors for his efforts last season, averaging 33.2 points and 5.8 assists per game on 53.1 percent shooting from the field and 46.2 percent from three. In the final against the Spurs, Brunson had 25 points, four rebounds and eight assists and was a plus-15 in the 124-113 win for the Knicks. Simply put, when the stakes get highest, Brunson seems to elevate his game to another level. When a player is as masterful as he is at getting to his spots, drawing fouls and hitting tough shots, and he's able to lock in with bigger stakes on the line, he becomes extremely tough to stop, as is the case with the southpaw bucket-getting floor general.

Stats: 30.2 ppg, 13.4 rpg, 9.7 apg, 1.5 spg, 0.9 bpg, 59.1 FG%, 53.5 3P%

Newfound Nikola Jokic detractors, who have started to cling to his lack of team success since the Denver Nuggets' 2022-23 championship, aren't going to love this, but we ranked Jokic among the five best NBA Cup performers ever despite the fact that he's never been able to lead Denver past the group stage of the competition. And can you blame us? Just look at his numbers. Jokic ranks fifth all-time in NBA Cup points per game, second in rebounds and third in assists, as his typical statistical dominance has translated to the league's three-year-old mid-season tournament. Alas, Jokic hasn't gotten enough help from teammates to get further in the competition as of yet, though that could very well change this season.

Stats: 22.4 ppg, 8.3 rpg, 8.1 apg, 1.0 spg, 0.4 bpg, 52.4 FG%, 42.1 3P%

Had LeBron James kept up his pace from his first NBA Cup appearance, back when it was called the In-Season Tournament in 2023-24, he'd be the unquestioned best player in the competition's history. That NBA Cup, James led the Lakers to the championship, was named MVP of the tournament and made the All-Tournament Team after averaging 26.4 points, 8.0 rebounds, 7.6 assists and 1.6 steals. After that, James' NBA Cup run dwindled, as the four-time league MVP would average just 17.8 points in the competition in 2024-25 and 19.0 points in last year's edition, which hurt his place in this ranking. James and Co. didn't get past the group stage of the NBA Cup in '25 and were eliminated in the quarterfinal in '26, so after James' fiery start in the competition's history, his output wasn't the same the next two times he participated. Even then, James will always be remembered as the first MVP and the first champion in the Cup's history. James had a 24-point, 11-rebound, four-assist outing in L.A.'s championship game win over the Pacers back in 2024, a 123-109 Lakers victory.

Stats: 28.0 ppg, 4.4 rpg, 7.7 apg, 0.9 spg, 0.3 bpg, 49.3 FG%, 48.5 3P%

Accolades : One NBA Cup title, one All-Tournament Team selection

The 2025 NBA Cup proved that, at least for a bit, the Antetokounmpo partnership with Damian Lillard did work, as the Bucks won their three knockout-round games that year by a combined 29 points, including an impressive 97-81 demolition of the eventual champion Thunder in the championship game. In that contest, Lillard went off for 23 points on 12 field-goal attempts, four rebounds and four assists. Overall in that NBA Cup run, Lillard averaged 27.3 points and 8.3 assists on 45.9 percent shooting from three. It's too bad Lillard got injured in that subsequent NBA playoff run, as he and his Greek counterpart could have made some noise that postseason, based on how well they performed together in the NBA Cup.

Stats: 23.4 ppg, 13.3 rpg, 4.3 apg, 1.0 spg, 2.8 bpg, 54.5 FG%, 70.5 FT%

Former No. 1 pick Anthony Davis was still at his two-way peak in 2024 when he and James led the Lakers to the In-Season Tournament championship. Davis was an absolute force on both ends of the floor, finishing explosively around the basket offensively and using his 7-foot-5 wingspan to block just about everything on the other end of the floor. Although James won NBA Cup MVP that year, Davis was the best player in the championship game win over the Pacers, going off for 41 points, 20 rebounds, five assists and four blocks on 16-of-24 shooting in the 123-109 victory over Indiana. Only two players have put up such a stat line in a regular-season game: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Joe Barry Carroll — which speaks to how dominant Davis was that night.

Stats: 28.9 ppg, 4.9 rpg, 7.3 apg, 1.7 spg, 0.5 bpg, 47.0 FG%, 38.3 3P%

De'Aaron Fox's most dominant Cup days came with the Sacramento Kings in 2023-24 and 2024-25. In those NBA Cup campaigns, respectively, Fox averaged 34.5 points, 7.3 rebounds and 7.5 assists per game, followed by 33.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 6.5 assists, although he was only able to lead Sacramento out of the group stage once, in 2024, when the Kings fell in the quarterfinal, 127-117, at the hands of the New Orleans Pelicans. Once he was with the Spurs, Fox's numbers fell to a more humble 22.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 2.0 steals per game in last season's NBA Cup. Fox helped lead San Antonio all the way to the championship game, where the Spurs fell 124-113 to the New York Knicks. In what proved to be a preview of the NBA Finals, Fox struggled against New York in the championship game, scoring 16 points and dishing out nine assists while going just 5-of-13 from the floor and giving away five turnovers.

Stats: 22.1 ppg, 11.9 rpg, 3.1 apg, 0.8 spg, 0.9 bpg, 47.9 FG%, 39.9 3P%

Accolades : One NBA Cup championship, one All-Tournament Team selection

The Knicks swept the main team awards last season, winning both the NBA championship and the NBA Cup title, and big man Karl-Anthony Towns had a lot to do with that, performing at a high level in both competitions. Towns is a fantastic face-up scorer for a big man, a pretty much elite three-point shooter and a high-level rebounder, making him a problem on both ends of the floor. Towns has also done a great job of figuring out his role on the Brunson-led Knicks, becoming hyper-efficient by choosing his spots well. In the Knicks' NBA Cup semifinal win over the Orlando Magic last year, the victory that got them to the championship game, Towns had a huge outing, scoring 29 points on nine-of-11 shooting, securing eight rebounds and hitting two three-pointers. Brunson gets a lot of the credit for New York's recent success, but people shouldn't sleep on what a high-level player Towns is.

articles.title: Kobe Bryant's Game-Worn Lower Merion HS Jersey Sets Record at Auction, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: A game-worn high school jersey from Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant sold for more than $2 million at auction.
articles.body:
A game-worn high school jersey from Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant sold for more than $2 million at auction.

Cllct's Darren Rovell noted how much the jersey had risen in value:

The $2.2 million price tag is the highest-ever for a high school jersey and nearly double the previous record. The St. Vincent-St. Mary's jersey LeBron James donned for his famous Sports Illustrated cover reached $1.3 million at auction in 2024.

Bryant's exploits at Lower Merion High School in Pennsylvania made him a national star before he arrived in the NBA. As a senior, he was a McDonald's All-American and earned multiple national player of the year honors.

The Charlotte Hornets selected Bryant 13th overall in the 1996 NBA draft but traded him to the Lakers for Vlade Divac. Bryant preferred to land in L.A., and general manager Jerry West recognized early on the teenager had the potential to be special.

Needless to say, West was proven correct.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham makes ’20 seconds’ anthem plea as WNBA Finals reach Game 6
articles.summary: The Fever guard says the Dream skipped the anthem against Indiana in August, long before President Donald Trump called for a WNBA boycott during the Finals.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von that WNBA teams leaving the court for the national anthem is nothing new this season, and the pending free agent tied her stance to military families and a call for more unity among players.

"This has been happening throughout the whole season," Cunningham said on This Past Weekend. "People are just kind of getting mad about it now." She added, "I take a lot of pride in where I come from, and I'm proud to be an American citizen ."

What does Cunningham do during the national anthem?

The 30-year-old guard pointed to relatives who wore the uniform. "We have family members who have served, and they're over there doing things that are unimaginable for us to be out here living our dreams," she said.

"So anytime that I can shout out our veterans and the people who are currently fighting for us, I'm going to show that support," Cunningham said. "That doesn't mean that's where everyone stands."

She also boiled the moment down to a simple request. "Okay, this isn't about me. I need 20 seconds of your best behavior," she said.

Cunningham has seen the walkouts from the floor. When Indiana visited Atlanta on Aug. 18, Dream players stayed off the court for the anthem while the Fever lined up and Cunningham held her hand over her heart, prompting Alabama Sen. Tommy Tuberville to post, "Sophie Cunningham is a true PATRIOT ."

The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court before the anthem at Game 1 of the Finals on Oct. 17 at Chase Center and returned about two minutes later, a routine both teams kept through the series.

The 2026 WNBA rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to " stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line" during the anthem. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said, "We're two years in. That's been part of our pregame ."

Trump urged fans to tune out at an Iowa rally. "The NFL did that for a while, and they stopped because people stopped watching the games," Trump said. "So I think you should do the same thing with women's basketball."

Golden State leads the series 3-2 entering Game 6, Valkyries at Dream, Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET in Atlanta.

Von asked whether players feel pressure to take stands. "We have a lot of women in this league, and that doesn't mean we're all going to agree," Cunningham said. "I think we need more unifying."

The former Missouri standout is an unrestricted free agent after playing 2026 on a one-year, $665,000 deal. Indiana also parted ways with general manager Amber Cox and team president Kelly Krauskopf after a first-round playoff exit, so a new front office will decide whether to bring her back.
